difficulty_reason: Fiberwise contraction does not by itself control entropy because short loops can repeatedly leave fibers while the metric degenerates. The authors construct face-coherent Lipschitz retractions on uniform neighborhoods and prove an arc-to-edge deformation with a length constant independent of the collapsing parameter. They then count the interleaved long edges and fiber paths using subgroup growth to obtain the required entropy bound, which combines with volume scaling to give the strict codimension threshold.
